next_steps: Run /plan 710 to land the probe's five theorems as library declarations (new PlusSlicedCertificate/Limits/NoFiniteWidth.lean), restate the class's completeness in the module headers, and re-scope task 709 and the task 708 relay per the report's recommendations 1-4.

user_decision.question: The sliced certificate class is refuted for full L-plus AND for the CTL-like fragment (task 709's headline). Choose: (a) re-scope 709 to the 'finite width implies eventually periodic' theorem (report F4) or to a bounded-delay fragment, or abandon it; (b) have the 708 relay state the class is semantically incomplete (never-report-validity permanent for stab targets) rather than pending; (c) whether to file the regular-two-way-tree class as a research-first successor. Proceeding on the report's recommendations loses nothing meanwhile.
user_decision.recommendation: Land the probe as library theorems (recommendation 1), re-scope 709 to the F4 periodicity theorem, update the 708 relay wording, and defer the two-way-tree class until decidability of full L-plus is confirmed as a programme goal.

memory_candidates.content: Over Z-time, limit closure plus finite per-time fibres is Koenig's lemma: a certificate class presenting frames on Z x Fin n cannot certify a formula whose every model needs a universal eventuality (stab Fp at pre-states under the once-only clock theta) with unbounded delay at a single time. Witness Phi := theta' and Box(stab Fp -> not stab not Xp), probe NoFiniteWidthModel.lean. Finite carrier (theta) and finite width (Phi) are both refuted; the next presentation must have infinite fibres (regular two-way trees).

HWZ 2000 quasimodel technique transfers to L-plus only in its periodicity half: Theorem 14 (collapse the domain at each time to realised types) and Lemma 17 (splice at equal quasistates) both rely on every run condition being existential; L-plus's stab is a universal quantifier over runs, so the quasistate must carry one-sided (fwd/bwd) live sets and the pumping needs an idempotent Ramsey colour, not successive splicing.

Lean idiom: a regular Z-frame on a countable finitely branching bi-serial step relation is FrameOver.ofStep's construction with TaskFrame.saturation_of_fib_finite in place of saturation_of_finite, proving Fib (ofStepRel R) w d finite by induction on iter with Set.Finite.biUnion; and a Box-fact at one time transfers to every offset-0 path at every time via plusTruthAt_timeShift on worldHistoryOfStepPath.
